Easy way to save android phone battery

I'll save you some trouble visiting a site that you may or may not have heard of...

  • Uninstall apps that leave a service-type footprint. If you have AppOps/equivalent, just use that to make sure no permission is being abused that keeps the phone awake and "phoning home" (to the app dev's predetermined data-mining directions).

  • Keep that brightness down as low as you are comfortable with. Don't crank it right down if you don't like it, but keep it at Auto, or at least 50% max. Personally, my CM12 rom's Auto Bright at ~30% is plenty good for me (note3).

  • The worse you reception is to either WiFi or mobile data, or both, the louder your phone needs to scream to be heard. Make sure you have good reception on either connection type. Better yet, as often as you aren't using one or the other connection, disable it. Tasker could be useful here.

  • Get rid of all-things google. This is a big one, since it's so ingrained in the android ecosystem and isn't exactly easy for anyone to do. But believe you me, again using CM12 (or cyanogenmod generally) as an example, is entirely possible to ditch google. Google Play Services is a monster of a battery drain. There are all kinds of alternatives for every service that google offers.

  • If you aren't using: NFC, Bluetooth, and more importanly Location Services, turn that shit off. With Location service-stuffs, unless you forsee needing to visit your location history, just keep it off and enable it on demand. Don't leave it on always reporting additional location data. I don't mean to protect privacy, but it's another service that keeps pumping out data.

  • If you want to keep your battery healthy, do not let it ever fall lower than 50% charge. Hell, keep the charge "topped up" as often as you are able without switching up your routine. A complete battery discharge adds unnecessary on the battery, the tech doesn't work that way anymore. And you don't need to worry tooooooooo much about 'over charging' the battery, the battery itself can regulate itself when it's full. I'm on mobile, but I highly recommend checking out a wiki on how the battery works, I can't remember the name of the battery tech but I think phones (and a shit tonne of other electronics out there) use lithium-ion? The only exception is, maybe every month or two, allow the phone to completely discharge until power off. Plug it into a 500mA charger (or into a computer) to charge back up to 100%, then power up the phone. All this will allow for is to ensure the phone recognizes the charge level normally.

  • Don't clear you recent tabs/apps. Just don't. Android can very efficiently manage apps. Don't be fooled into believing that more unused ram is better. Quite the contrary.

That's all I can think of off the top of my head. Maybe now I'll check out the site. After archive.is'ing it that is ;)

Anyone, feel free to correct me on anything, it's been a couple of years since I went deep into understanding battery saving on my device.

Train wreck at Montparnasse Station. Paris. 1895.

This accident occurred at 4 pm on October 22, 1895 when the Granville–Paris Express overran the buffer stop at its Gare Montparnasse terminus. With the train several minutes late and the driver trying to make up for lost time, it entered the station too fast and the train air brake failed. After running through the buffer stop, the train crossed the 30-metre (100 ft) wide station concourse and crashed through the station wall. The locomotive fell onto the Place de Rennes below, where it stood on its nose. A woman in the street below was killed by falling masonry. The locomotive was found to have suffered little damage.
